raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #48172.

`--tool-call-parser=auto` resolved to *no parser* for the chat templates that use the plain-JSON tool-call format, so tool calls came back as plain text with `tool_calls: null`:

```
--tool-call-parser=auto specified but could not detect tool-call parser from chat template. Disabling tool-call parser.
```

Affected templates (all of them document the format and none of them has an `enable_thinking` toggle):

- `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (and 7B / 32B / 72B / Coder / Math)
- `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`
- `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct`
- `Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct`
- `inclusionAI/Ling-mini-2.0`, `inclusionAI/Ring-mini-linear-2.0`

The format is:

```
<tool_call>
{"name": "...", "arguments": {...}}
</tool_call>
```

The `qwen` detection rule keys on an `enable_thinking` toggle defaulting to `true`, which is how the Qwen3 templates that *do* have a toggle get detected. The templates above have no toggle at all, so nothing matched and the tool-call parser was disabled.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/parser/template_detection.py`: add a `_is_qwen_json_tool_call` predicate and a `qwen_json_tool_call` rule to `TOOL_CALL_PARSER_RULES`, mapping the plain-JSON format to the `qwen` parser (`Qwen25Detector`), which reads exactly this format.
  - The rule recognizes the format by its tool-call tag plus the JSON `"name"` key. The key appears either escaped (`\"name\":`) where the template documents the format inside a Jinja string literal, or plain (`"name":`) where the template renders a tool call back to the model; both forms are accepted.
  - The rule is placed after the `qwen` rule, so templates that *do* have an `enable_thinking` toggle keep resolving through `qwen` as before, and before the broad `deepseek_v3` / `deepseek_r1` fallbacks.
- `test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py`:
  - `test_plain_json_tool_call_format_detects_qwen_parser`: the escaped and the plain JSON-key shapes both resolve to `qwen`.
  - `test_tool_call_tag_without_json_name_is_not_qwen`: the XML-KV tool format (GLM style) shares the tool-call tag but has no JSON payload, so the new rule must not claim it.
  - `test_qwen25_plain_json_template_detects_qwen_tool_call_parser`: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` resolves to the `qwen` tool-call parser and to no reasoning parser.
  - `test_specific_rules_precede_broad_fallbacks`: asserts the new rule's position relative to `qwen` and `deepseek_v3`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: this only changes which tool-call parser `--tool-call-parser=auto` selects. It does not touch model, sampling, or serving code paths.

The selected parser was checked against the format the affected templates document:

```
<tool_call>
{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}
</tool_call>
```

which `Qwen25Detector` parses into `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Paris"}}` (same detector that `--tool-call-parser qwen25` selects; `qwen25` is an alias of `qwen`).

To bound the blast radius, the detection was diffed before/after this change over the chat templates *and* the real tokenizer vocabs of 41 models on the Hub:

- every template that already resolved to a parser still resolves to the **same** parser (no template changed from one parser to another);
- the templates listed above, which previously resolved to *no* parser, now resolve to `qwen`;
- the reasoning parser is unchanged for every model.

```
unchanged: 24, changed: 13, no template: 4
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: one extra rule, evaluated once at server startup.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A: no user-facing flag or behavior change.)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A: see above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Note on the second request in #48172

The issue also asks for a louder signal when `auto` finds no tool-call parser for a template that does take `tools` (failing at startup, or saying so in the response). That is a behavior change with a wider surface, so it is left out of this PR and kept as a follow-up.

@@ -498,6 +498,22 @@ def _is_qwen3_coder(ctx):
     return ctx.has_text("<function=") and ctx.has_text("<parameter=")
 
 
+def _is_qwen_json_tool_call(ctx):
+    # Plain-JSON tool-call format:
+    #   <tool_call>\n{"name": "...", "arguments": {...}}\n</tool_call>
+    # Used by the Qwen2.5 / Qwen3-Instruct / Ling-mini chat templates. Those
+    # templates have no ``enable_thinking`` toggle, so the qwen3 rule (which
+    # keys on that toggle) cannot fire for them and they fell through to "no
+    # tool-call parser", which returns tool calls as plain text.
+    #
+    # The JSON key appears either escaped (``\"name\":``) where the template
+    # documents the format inside a Jinja string literal, or plain
+    # (``"name":``) where the template renders a tool call back to the model.
+    return ctx.has_text("<tool_call>") and (
+        ctx.has_text('"name":') or ctx.has_text('\\"name\\":')
+    )
+
+
 def _is_qwen3(ctx):
     return ctx.reasoning_config == ReasoningToggleConfig(
         toggle_param="enable_thinking", default_enabled=True
@@ -619,6 +635,9 @@ def _is_iquest_q1(ctx):
     DetectionRule(name="mimo", value="mimo", predicate=_is_mimo),
     DetectionRule(name="qwen3_coder", value="qwen3_coder", predicate=_is_qwen3_coder),
     DetectionRule(name="qwen", value="qwen", predicate=_is_qwen3),
+    DetectionRule(
+        name="qwen_json_tool_call", value="qwen", predicate=_is_qwen_json_tool_call
+    ),
     DetectionRule(name="deepseek_v3", value="deepseekv3", predicate=_is_deepseek_v3),
     DetectionRule(name="deepseek_r1", value="deepseekv3", predicate=_is_deepseek_r1),
 )

@@ -704,6 +704,55 @@ def test_qwen3_detects_qwen_tool_call_parser(self):
         self.assertEqual(rp, "qwen3")
         self.assertEqual(tcp, "qwen")
 
+    def test_plain_json_tool_call_format_detects_qwen_parser(self):
+        # The Qwen2.5 / Qwen3-Instruct / Ling-mini chat templates document the
+        # plain-JSON tool-call format and carry no enable_thinking toggle, so
+        # the qwen3 rule (which keys on that toggle) cannot fire for them and
+        # they used to fall through to "no tool-call parser".
+        templates = {
+            # The format is documented inside a Jinja string literal, where
+            # the JSON quotes are escaped.
+            "escaped_json_key": (
+                '{{- "\\n<tool_call>\\n{\\"name\\": <function-name>, '
+                '\\"arguments\\": <args-json-object>}\\n</tool_call>\\n" }}'
+            ),
+            # The template renders a tool call back to the model, where the
+            # JSON quotes are not escaped.
+            "plain_json_key": (
+                "{%- for tool_call in message.tool_calls %}\n"
+                '{{- \'\\n<tool_call>\\n{"name": "\' }}\n'
+                "{{- tool_call.name }}\n"
+                '{{- \'", "arguments": \' }}\n'
+                "{{- tool_call.arguments | tojson }}\n"
+                "{{- '}\\n</tool_call>' }}\n"
+                "{%- endfor %}"
+            ),
+        }
+        for name, template in templates.items():
+            with self.subTest(name=name):
+                force, config = detect_reasoning_pattern(template)
+                result = detect_tool_call_parser(
+                    template, _DummyTokenizer([]), config, force
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(result, "qwen")
+
+    def test_tool_call_tag_without_json_name_is_not_qwen(self):
+        # The XML-KV tool format (GLM style) shares the tool-call tag but has
+        # no JSON payload, so the plain-JSON rule must not claim it.
+        template = (
+            "<tool_call>get_weather\n"
+            "<arg_key>city</arg_key><arg_value>Paris</arg_value>\n"
+            "</tool_call>"
+        )
+        force, config = detect_reasoning_pattern(template)
+        result = detect_tool_call_parser(template, _DummyTokenizer([]), config, force)
+        self.assertIsNone(result)
+
+    def test_qwen25_plain_json_template_detects_qwen_tool_call_parser(self):
+        rp, tcp = self._detect_all("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")
+        self.assertIsNone(rp)
+        self.assertEqual(tcp, "qwen")
+
